## ISEN691 Syllabus

Section 202 (12682) Research Summer 2026 - College Station

## Catalog Description

Research. Credit 1 or more each semester. Research in industrial engineering field; content and credit dependent upon needs of individual student.

## Additional Course Details

This research study will follow an ongoing project in the Human Factors & Cognitive Systems (HF&CS) Lab. Ideally the research efforts will play out over multiple semesters, ultimately concluding in (or including) a full human subjects data collection. After data collection is complete, the student will lead the efforts in analyzing the data and writing a final research report, for submission to peerreviewed journal outlets (to be determined in consultation with Dr. Ferris and HF&CS members).

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- Complete the processes of achieving IRB approval and conducting human subjects study

- Analyze collected data and produce results for statistical testing

- Acquire a deeper understanding of the mechanisms involved in human perception

- Develop a procedure for reliably inducing human performance effects, based on analyzed results

- Communicate technical results through periodic lab presentations and the submission of research for peer-reviewed publication

None

## Grading Policy

### Grading Policy

Midterm deliverable

: 30% of grade

50% of grade

Weekly meeting attendance and updates:

20% of grade

### Grading Scale

A = 90-100%

B = 80-89%

C = 70-79%

D = 60-69%

F = <60%

### Expected Outcomes/Deliverables

The grade for this course will be determined by the following deliverables:

1. Midterm deliverable (due Week 8): Presentation to HF&CS lab on initial progress of data collection with analysis
2. Final Deliverable (due Finals Week): Final report with progress of entire project
3. Attend weekly meetings with the HF&CS lab team and the larger Rubberhand project team, give regular updates on progress in conducting the human subjects study, and analyzing/reporting its results.

## Grading Appeals:

Every effort will be made to ensure that grading is as objective and fair as possible. If you believe that there is an error in the grading, please submit, in writing, an appeal within one week of your work being returned. However, please be advised that if you submit such an appeal, the entire assignment/exam will be regraded to ensure that all parts are properly graded. As such, your grade on the exam could increase or decrease based on the secondary grading.

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).
